extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and grant reviewers evaluating RPG (R01/R03/R15/R21/R34) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for peer reviewers on evaluating Research Project Grant (RPG) applications (R01, R03, R15, R21, R34), including definitions of review criteria, considerations for specific mechanisms, and special topic assessments (human subjects, animals, biohazards, resource sharing, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed). For R15, reviewers will assess likelihood to make an important scientific contribution, provide research opportunities to students, and strengthen the institution's research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider all review criteria and additional considerations when assessing likelihood of sustained, powerful influence. Note mechanism-specific emphases: R15 adds focus on student opportunities and institutional research environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: R03 (Small Research Grant) Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R03 supports discrete, well-defined projects realistically completable in two years with limited funding; applications may not contain extensive detail or discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach. Appropriate justification can come from literature citations, other-source data, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, especially for pilot/feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 (AREA) Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R15 objectives: (1) support meritorious research, (2) strengthen research environment of schools not major NIH recipients, (3) expose undergrad/grad students to meritorious research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are not required but may be included. Reviewers should consider whether, if funded, the award will substantially strengthen the school/academic component and expose students to research.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 (Exploratory/Developmental) Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R21 supports investigation of novel ideas or new models/tools/technologies with potential for significant impact; applications need not have extensive background/preliminary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should focus on conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to advance knowledge. Justification may be literature citations, other-source data, or investigator data when available. Preliminary data are not required but may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: R34 (Clinical Trial Planning Grant) Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R34 supports development of Phase III clinical trials: team establishment, data management/oversight tools, recruitment strategy definition, protocol finalization, and operations manual preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not designed for collection of preliminary data or pilot studies to support trial rationale. Reviewers should focus evaluation on the rationale for the proposed clinical trial and the design/protocol in its current, early form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will completion change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventive interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R15 also consider whether the AREA award will substantially affect the school/academic component by strengthening research environment and exposing students to research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? For Early Stage Investigators or those early in independent careers, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated ongoing accomplishments advancing their fields? For collaborative/multi-PD/PI projects, do investigators have complementary/integrated expertise and appropriate leadership, governance, and organizational structure?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R15 additionally consider whether PD(s)/PI(s) have suitable experience supervising students in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge or seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions? Are the concepts/approaches/instrumentation novel to one field or novel in a broad sense? Is a refinement, improvement, or new application proposed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess degree to which the project proposes novel elements or paradigm shifts rather than incremental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented? If early-stage, will the strategy establish feasibility and manage particularly risky aspects?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research are involved, evaluate plans for protection of human subjects from research risks and justification for inclusion/exclusion based on sex/gender, race, ethnicity, and children. For R15 clinical research language is similar. For early-stage projects emphasize feasibility and risk management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment where the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment and other physical resources adequate? Will the project benefit from unique features of the environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R15 also evaluate availability of well-qualified students to participate and evidence that students have or will pursue careers in biomedical/behavioral sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For research involving human subjects (not exempt under 45 CFR Part 46), committees evaluate justification for involvement and proposed protections from research risk according to five review criteria: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to subjects and others, (4) importance of knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials. For exempt research, evaluate justification for exemption, human subjects involvement/characteristics, and sources of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH 'Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects' for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposed project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, committees will evaluate proposed plans for inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals based on sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, and inclusion (or exclusion) of children to determine if justified in terms of scientific goals and strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH 'Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research' for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee will evaluate involvement of live vertebrate animals according to five points: (1) proposed use and species/strains/ages/sex/numbers, (2) justifications for use and appropriateness of species/numbers, (3) adequacy of veterinary care, (4) procedures for limiting discomfort/distress/pain/injury including use of analgesic/anesthetic/tranquilizing drugs and restraining devices, and (5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the 'Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section' for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hazards are identified, determine whether adequate protection is proposed (biosafety, biocontainment, procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adequacy of responses to prior review and whether criticisms have been addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate documented accomplishments, productivity, and how prior objectives were met during the past support period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project. If the revision relates to a line of investigation in the original application not recommended for approval previously, the committee will consider whether responses to previous review comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are evident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the revision is justified and whether previous concerns have been sufficiently addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries and either are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider special opportunities and whether foreign components add unique value to the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess information provided about Select Agent(s) including: (1) the Select Agent(s) to be used, (2) registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, (3) procedures to monitor possession/use/transfer of Select Agent(s), and (4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that adequate biosafety, biocontainment, and security measures are described and that registration/compliance issues are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the following Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing, are reasonable: (1) Data Sharing Plan; (2) Sharing Model Organisms; and (3) Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS)/Genomic Data Sharing Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the plans or stated rationales for not sharing are reasonable and appropriate for the proposed research and community benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate cost realism, appropriateness of requested duration, and whether resources requested align with scope of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section to give constructive feedback, identify major deficiencies, or advise on whether substantial revision is required prior to resubmission.
